classification.difficultyReason: Combine ordinates of two absolute-value graphs, tracking changes in gradient at both vertices.

answer.worked:
Add the ordinates of the two component graphs at each $x$. At $x=0,1,2$, the sums are all $2$. For $x<0$, both component graphs have gradient $-1$, so their sum has gradient $-2$. For $x>2$, both have gradient $1$, so their sum has gradient $2$.

Draw the horizontal segment from $(0,2)$ to $(2,2)$, with an upward ray extending left from $(0,2)$ and an upward ray extending right from $(2,2)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher evidence, printed page 322, top-left Q4(a)
spec.description: Horizontal segment at y=2 between x=0 and x=2, joined continuously to upward rays; black axes and labelled ticks at x=2 and y=2; no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=|x|+|x-2|; gradients -2, 0 and 2 on the three consecutive intervals.
